corrections.text: The Overview attributes to SDxCentral that vendors are pushing 1.6T Ethernet into 'AI clusters that are expanding from thousands to hundreds of thousands of accelerators.' That scaling figure comes from Arista's own press release ('As AI workloads scale from thousands to hundreds of thousands of XPUs'), not from the cited SDxCentral article, which describes only a 'growing cohort of vendors offering 1.6 Tb/s networking switches' with no accelerator counts.

The Analysis states 'SDxCentral notes that Ethernet is expanding into scale-up networking, the domain long dominated by Nvidia's NVLink.' The cited SDxCentral article does not discuss scale-up networking or NVLink; it references scale-out AI fabrics. The scale-up framing traces to Arista's press release and Network World, and the NVLink comparison does not appear in any cited source.
The article describes the 7060XE7-64PRS-RV3-L as a '2RU' liquid-cooled switch. Arista's press release specifies a '2OU' (ORv3 Open Rack Unit) form factor, which differs from a standard 2RU rack unit.
